thread.title: Jaguars Beat Ravens 33-10, Improve to 6-2

author: ethan.brook News Editor
title: Jaguars Beat Ravens 33-10, Improve to 6-2
text:
The Jacksonville Jaguars defeated the Baltimore Ravens 33-10 on Thursday night at M&T Bank Stadium, overcoming heavy rain to improve their record to 6-2.
Joe Fagnano starts for injured Ravens quarterbacks
Undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano made his first NFL start on Thursday Night Football due to injuries to Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley. The Ravens also recently added former Bears quarterback Austin Reed, who was in Chicago during the 2025 offseason, to serve as the QB2 behind Fagnano, according to Sports. Yahoo.com.
Fagnano struggled throughout the contest, completing 10 of 18 passes for 60 yards and throwing two interceptions, the sources noted. One interception was caught by Jaguars defensive back Buster Brown on a third-and-long attempt, which allowed Jacksonville to take over deep in Baltimore territory at the 26-yard line, NBC Sports reported.
Henry had 12 carries for 51 yards and threw a pass that resulted in a 3-yard loss, ESPN noted.
Jaguars offense capitalizes on Baltimore turnovers
Jacksonville's offense used multiple opportunities to build a lead. Running back Bhayshul Tuten, who was questionable with foot and ankle injuries, scored a 1-yard touchdown on the Jaguars’ opening drive, ESPN reported. Tuten finished the game with 22 yards on eight carries.
After Malaki Starks hit Jaguars two-way player Travis Hunter, causing a bobble of Trevor Lawrence’s pass, Washington secured the catch and ran 50 yards for a touchdown with 58 seconds remaining in the half, NBC Sports stated. This play helped the Jaguars lead 17-3 at halftime.
Trevor Lawrence finished the night completing 9-of-15 passes for 197 yards and one touchdown, according to NBC Sports. Lawrence entered the game with a 105.0 passer rating, ESPN reported.
The Jaguars’ receiving attack featured Jakobi Meyers with four catches for 65 yards, Parker Washington with two catches for 61 yards, and rookie tight end Nate Boerkircher with one catch for 52 yards, NBC Sports noted. For the Jacksonville defense, linebacker Foyesade Oluokun led the team with six tackles and a sack, NBC Sports reported.
Baltimore struggles with scoring and penalties
The loss marks a difficult stretch for first-year head coach Jesse Minter. The team currently leads the NFL with 24 false starts.
In the third quarter, tight end Mark Andrews fumbled a snap on 4th-and-1, resulting in a turnover on downs while the team trailed 20-3, ESPN reported. Kicker Cam Little extended the Jaguars’ lead with a field goal through the rain, NBC Sports noted.
The Ravens’ roster also dealt with several absences and injuries. Cornerback Nate Wiggins was inactive due to illness.
Individual performances from the matchup
Key individual performances from the matchup are detailed below:
| Player | Team | Stat Line |
|---|---|---|
| Trevor Lawrence | Jaguars | 9-of-15, 197 passing yards, 1 TD |
| Joe Fagnano | Ravens | 10-of-18, 60 passing yards, 2 INT |
| Bhayshul Tuten | Jaguars | 8 carries, 22 rushing yards, 1 TD |
| Derrick Henry | Ravens | 12 carries, 51 rushing yards |
Upcoming schedule for Baltimore and Jacksonville
The Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) enter the next week following a 42-7 victory over the Indianapolis Colts at EverBank Stadium, ESPN reported. The Baltimore Ravens (4-5) are scheduled to play the Los Angeles Chargers on Nov. 16 at 8:15 p.m. ET, USA TODAY noted. There are reports that Baltimore expects to finalize a trade for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett this weekend, though he would not be available until next week, USA TODAY and Sports. Yahoo.com stated.

Running back Bhayshul Tuten, who was questionable with foot and ankle injuries, scored a 1-yard touchdown on the Jaguars’ opening drive, ESPN reported.
